main_body: Grey stone mortar bowl with a green herb filling and a brown wooden pestle angled out of it
top_band: Light grey rim ellipse with green contents at about rows 7-10 (about 4 rows), then a step to the mid-grey bowl body
evidence: Reading down the middle column: the light grey rim and green herb interior form an elliptical opening about 4 rows tall (rows 7-10). A lighter rim edge follows, then the darker grey bowl body and foot (rows 11-15). The inside of the opening is visible as a green filling, so it reads as a bowl seen from above with a front face below. The ellipse is small but it is a real horizontal surface, not a rim-only line. The pestle is a small detail.

style.evidence: The bowl body uses about 3 grey tones (light rim, mid body, dark base) with little grain. The grey body is a flat fill of roughly 5x4 pixels or more with no speckle or stone texture. The dark outline is largely neutral dark grey, with some brown near the pestle. The pestle is a near-flat brown with a single highlight. Compared with the roofed well and cheese stall, which carry rich tile shading, roof scallops and stone-by-stone shading, the candidate is much thinner and sticker-like.
